turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I've got fifteen minutes, Hale. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of your class. Nobody called me first, so start there.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
Don't thank me. You didn't call me, and I'm here because my son came home upset. Why was the zero entered before anyone spoke to Owen or to me?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.
A machine's guess, Hale. Ninety-four percent from a checker is an opinion, not a fact. Who looked at the essay besides the software, and did anyone ask Owen about it first?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.

"Quite reliable." On what basis? I'm asking because the company that sells that software says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. Is there anything else you have, or is the checker all you've got?
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to" is not a policy, Hale. Your own school procedure says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. Which part of that did you think didn't apply?
I hope you understand my position.
I understand that you entered a zero and didn't call me first. Tell me what you have that shows Owen wrote something he didn't write, or take the zero off.
